title: Dispatch: Fix four PR #524 fresh-review defects (position chronology, seam position authority, recurring-question rulings, ruling multiplicity)
description:
Dispatch for PR #524 fresh-full-review findings (GitHub review #5097622281, exact head 0479116, semantic-system profile). FOUR blocking defects spanning eshyra-jhpt.1, .2 and .3, plus closing eshyra-neus. All four were independently reproduced by the supervisor at 0479116; probe output is quoted so you can write tests that fail today. Fix all four on ONE head — the reviewer requires a fresh full review after any material repair, so batching gives one review cycle instead of four.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev2 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev2, cut from the integration branch eshyra-jhpt at 0479116 (the reviewed head). npm ci has already been run there and @eshyra/core resolves into the worktree; AGENTS.md now REQUIRES this and verify:worktree enforces it. Work only inside that worktree.

=============================================================
DEFECT 1 (owner eshyra-jhpt.3, breaks eshyra-jhpt.8's contract)
Abandoned turns permanently consume campaign chronology.
=============================================================
runTurn calls resolveCampaignPosition BEFORE `SAVEPOINT eshyra_turn`, and resolveCampaignPosition commits its own transaction. A terminal turn failure rolls back only to that savepoint, so the abandoned attempt KEEPS its ordinal. The real CLI producer (packages/cli/src/playTurnLoop.ts) then reports the failure and calls `deps.nextId('turn')` again for the next input, so the next canonical turn gets a LATER ordinal with a dead attempt wedged between two canonical turns.
campaignRules.ts checkTemporalMode defines immediacy as `disputedPosition.ordinal + 1 === currentPosition.ordinal`, so a single provider/model/audit failure makes the genuinely previous adjudication ineligible for disputed-turn timing.

REPRODUCED at 0479116:
    canonical A=1  abandoned=2  next canonical C=3
    disputed-turn rule targeting A while current is C -> "disputed-turn mode may target only the current or immediately preceding turn"

REQUIRED PROPERTIES (the design choice is yours; state your reasoning in your notes):
  - An abandoned/failed attempt must not affect canonical turn adjacency.
  - A deliberate replay of a disputed turn must still reuse that turn's existing position (this is why resolveCampaignPosition sits before the savepoint — do not move it without preserving that).
  - eshyra-jhpt.8 says abandoned adjudication MAY remain diagnostic/provenance history but must not be continuing campaign canon, so deleting the evidence is acceptable only if you can still satisfy that; marking the row non-canonical and computing adjacency over canonical rows only is the more faithful reading.
  - If adjacency must be computed against persisted state rather than raw ordinal arithmetic, changing the eshyra-jhpt.1 domain contract is IN SCOPE here (that bead is reopened for this) — e.g. resolving the previous canonical position and passing it in, instead of comparing ordinals directly. Keep the two temporal modes as they are.
EVIDENCE: an integration regression through the REAL runTurn / turn-id lifecycle — a successful canonical turn, then a forced terminal failure, then the next successful turn — proving canonical adjacency survives, plus proof that an intended replay reuses the existing position rather than allocating a new one. Exercise the persistence table and the actually returned positions, not checkTemporalMode in isolation.

=============================================================
DEFECT 2 (owner eshyra-jhpt.2)
The DB-backed read seam can mix two campaign positions in one run.
=============================================================
createCampaignRuleReadSeam binds canonicalPosition and documents "binds a required campaign position so every query is replay-accurate", but activeRulesAtPosition honours a per-call `query.campaignPosition` override while activeRulingsForAmbiguities always uses the bound one. discovery/campaignRuleSeam.ts joinCampaignRules DOES pass options.campaignPosition, so this is reachable, not a theoretical type state.

REPRODUCED at 0479116 (seam bound at P10):
    house rules with no override : [ 'house-early', 'house-late' ]
    same seam, override P5       : [ 'house-early' ]        <- different position
    activeRulingsForAmbiguities always uses the BOUND P10
This is the same temporal-divergence class already fixed once between house rules and rulings in the SQL predicate, now re-entering through the seam.

FIX: make campaign position single-authority across both methods. Either reject a per-call position that differs from the bound one with CampaignRuleError, or resolve one explicit position that both methods use. Do not leave a silent substitution.
EVIDENCE: construct a DB seam at one position, query it with another, and prove the contract either rejects the mismatch or returns the same historical slice from both methods.

=============================================================
DEFECT 3 (closes eshyra-neus; producer contract owned by .1/.2)
Recurring-question rulings fall through the discovery boundary entirely.
=============================================================
eshyra-jhpt.1 defines a ruling as EITHER a source-ambiguity resolution OR a stable recurring interpretation question. At the seam, a recurring-question ruling is returned by NEITHER method: activeRulesAtPosition filters to `ruleKind === 'house-rule'`, and activeRulingsForAmbiguities filters to ambiguity provenance.

REPRODUCED at 0479116 with one active recurring-question ruling:
    activeRulesAtPosition      : []   (house-rules only)
    activeRulingsForAmbiguities: []   (ambiguity-provenance only)
The complementary half is the open eshyra-neus defect: discovery/campaignRuleSeam.ts withRule casts EVERY ruleKind==='ruling' projection to CampaignRulingProjection, which is unsound for a recurring-question ruling that legitimately has no ambiguityId/selectedInterpretationId.

FIX both halves in this PR; the reviewer is explicit that a known fix-worthy defect is fixed in the current PR rather than deferred.
  - Producer: a recurring-question ruling must be returned by the seam. It cannot come from activeRulingsForAmbiguities (it has no ambiguity id), so activeRulesAtPosition is the correct carrier — i.e. that method returns active rules that are not ambiguity-linked rulings, rather than house rules only. Note the in-repo oracle fixture packages/core/test/discovery/support/oracleCampaignRules.ts pins the current house-rules-only shape because its cases only ever contain house rules and ambiguity rulings; update it in step with the real contract and say in your notes how you kept them consistent.
  - Consumer: withRule must classify by PROVENANCE, not by ruleKind alone — only an ambiguity-provenance projection may be treated as a CampaignRulingProjection. Do not fabricate ambiguityId/selectedInterpretationId to satisfy the type (a previous attempt did exactly that and it was rejected), and do not loosen CampaignRulingProjection.
EVIDENCE: persist a real recurring-question ruling, read it through the DB-backed seam, run it through joinCampaignRules, and assert it is retained in a semantically valid shape with no fabricated ambiguity fields. The test must fail against 0479116. Then close eshyra-neus with a reason referencing this work.

=============================================================
DEFECT 4 (owner .1/.2 for the invariant, .3 must fail closed)
Two contradictory active rulings for one ambiguity are accepted, then silently collapsed.
=============================================================
Migration 0025 has no uniqueness constraint, createCampaignRule performs no sibling-active check, and listActiveRulingsForAmbiguitiesAtPosition can return several. assembleCampaignRulesContext then does rulingByAmbiguity.set(...) per row, so the last one silently wins the "Active ruling" slot — while `rules` still carries BOTH, so the rendered Campaign Rules section can show two contradictory rulings for the same ambiguity.

REPRODUCED at 0479116 (two active rulings on ambiguity:create-undead-ghast-wight-composition selecting mixed-within-total and homogeneous-alternative):
    ambiguity section shows exactly one "Active ruling": ruling-two
    but rules[] carries both: [ 'ruling-one', 'ruling-two' ]

FIX: close the multiplicity semantics. At most one ACTIVE ambiguity-provenance ruling per (campaignId, ambiguityId) at any position — enforce it in the store on create (and on any path that can produce an overlapping active interval), with CampaignRuleError. A partial unique index cannot express overlapping intervals on its own, so the admission check is the primary guard; add a DB constraint only if it genuinely helps. Separately, eshyra-jhpt.3 must FAIL CLOSED rather than silently collapsing if conflicting state ever reaches projection — do not let Map.set pick a winner.
If you believe scoped multiplicity is intentionally desirable, do not just allow it: represent it explicitly in the domain and make .3 preserve it, and justify that in your notes. Default expectation is the single-active-ruling invariant.
EVIDENCE: attempt two overlapping active rulings for one ambiguity and prove persistence rejects it; plus a historical supersession case proving the old ruling is still the active one before the successor's effective position and exactly one is active after it.

=============================================================
GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
=============================================================
- NEGATIVE PROOF, per defect: confirm each new regression test fails against 0479116 (check out the relevant file(s) from that commit into your worktree, observe the failures, restore your fix). Report the per-defect failure counts in your notes. Do not report a count you did not observe.
- Do not weaken any existing test or assertion to accommodate a fix. If an existing expectation is genuinely wrong under the corrected contract, say so explicitly in your notes with reasoning.
- Do not change the active-at-position SQL predicate, the position encoding, the migrations already merged, or anything outside these four defects.
- Scope note: .1, .2 and .3 are all reopened for this, so the domain model, the store and the context assembler are all editable where a defect requires it. Discovery (campaignRuleSeam.ts, discovery types, the oracle fixture) is editable ONLY for defect 3.

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing (it rewrites files). Report final pass/skip counts and confirm @eshyra/core resolves into this worktree.

Completion report for local commit 6759ccc on eshyra-jhpt.rev2. Fixed all four PR #524 fresh-review defects: runTurn now assigns positions inside the outer turn SAVEPOINT, so new failed attempts roll back their position while INSERT OR IGNORE preserves an existing replay position; the read seam rejects a per-call campaignPosition that differs from its bound position; activeRulesAtPosition carries house rules and recurring-question rulings, while discovery classifies campaignRulings only from ambiguity provenance; create admission rejects overlapping ambiguity-ruling intervals with CampaignRuleError (half-open intervals preserve valid supersession at the successor effective position), and assembleCampaignRulesContext fails closed on duplicate ambiguity projections. Updated the oracle seam and fixture contract for recurring-question rulings consistently. Negative proof: with relevant source files explicitly checked out from 0479116 and completed regression tests restored, npx vitest run on orchestrator.test.ts and campaignRuleStore.test.ts observed 6 failed / 60 passed tests: D1=1, D2=1, D3=2 (updated seam contract plus DB-seam/discovery join), D4=2 (admission plus fail-closed projection). No failure count is inferred. Post-fix targeted suite: 5 files, 115 passed. npm run verify:worktree passed: hidden Unicode/check/typecheck and 276 test files passed / 3 skipped, 4854 tests passed / 20 skipped. @eshyra/core resolved through this worktree to packages/core/dist/index.js and node_modules/@eshyra/core points to this worktree packages/core. No discovered follow-up bead was needed. Per defect 3, eshyra-neus is closed separately; this bead is ready for integration. No push, PR, or merge performed.
Supervisor review: all four fixes verified. Independently reproduced the negative proof (6 of 66 failures against 0479116, matching the reported per-defect split) and ran full verification. Merged to eshyra-jhpt at cc6d572.
